text: Mrs. Straker's account: one o'clock and seven o'clock
why: The story so far gives only the one o'clock wake-up. The seven o'clock time appears nowhere in the text read so far.
Paragraph 32 names Mrs. Straker, and paragraph 19 establishes Straker as a married man.
Paragraph 32 says he pulled on his large mackintosh before leaving the house.

text: Monday, later: the lads come back
why: Paragraph 32 says Hunter waited until his fellow-grooms had returned, after the Monday evening incident.
Paragraph 32 gives the time as one in the morning on the night following Monday's events, which is Tuesday.

text: Why did Straker go out at one in the morning?
why: A plain question the text has prompted, since Straker's departure is described and his stated reason is given.

text: Why did Straker go out at one in the morning? — to see that all was well
id: q.straker_aim=to see that all was well
why: Paragraph 32 records Straker's own stated intention to walk down and see that all was well, so the reader has reason to consider it.
